comparison: Perfect alignment on parasitism efficiency claims (C14-C29). Both evaluations recognize Td's superior performance on D. suzukii and characterize it as a major finding with strong experimental support.

Strong alignment on genome assembly claims (C30-C51). Both evaluations acknowledge genome sequencing as a key finding with comprehensive quality metrics. High Jaccard index (0.882) indicates near-complete overlap.

Good alignment on Timp gene family expansion (C52-C57, C148-C153). Both recognize this as a major finding. Peer review also includes functional claims (C72, C78, C144) showing broader grouping of venom-related findings.

Strong alignment on venom-induced developmental arrest (C62-C69). Both evaluations support the experimental evidence. Peer review extends to functional validation claims (C75-C77, C134), indicating broader integration of venom mechanism.

OpenEval focuses on functional validation of Timps using ectopic expression (C70-C78), while peer review groups venom characterization more broadly. Both support the findings but organize them differently.

Good alignment on teratocyte characterization (C79-C88). OpenEval focuses on morphological characterization, while peer review combines teratocyte identification with protease function (C89-C101, C135, C145), showing broader thematic grouping.

Strong alignment on teratocyte protease function (C89-C101). Both evaluations support the experimental evidence for tissue digestion. Jaccard index 0.5 shows substantial overlap with peer review's broader teratocyte grouping.
Good alignment on host age preference and parasitism efficiency (C102-C108). Both evaluations support these findings as major outcomes with strong experimental evidence.

Strong alignment on superparasitism benefits (C109-C113). Both evaluations recognize the experimental data showing improved outcomes. Peer review groups this with broader host age findings (C160-C164).

Good alignment on host discrimination behavior and ovipositor anatomy (C114-C122). Both evaluations support the behavioral and anatomical evidence. Peer review extends to transcriptomic characterization (C123-C130, C146).
Strong alignment on ovipositor transcriptomics and chemosensory function (C123-C130). Both evaluations support the expression profiling evidence distinguishing taste from olfactory reception.
Perfect alignment on gene duplication synthesis (C147, C154, C155). Both evaluations recognize this as a reasonable integrative interpretation tying together multiple gene family expansions.

Good alignment on molecular mechanism synthesis (C134-C139). Both evaluations accept the integration of venom and teratocyte findings into a coherent model, though peer review groups with broader synthetic claims (C17-C20, C170-C171).
Strong alignment on ecological interpretation of host age and superparasitism (C160-C164). Both evaluations support these conclusions as reasonable inferences from the behavioral data.

Good alignment on interspecific competition synthesis (C167-C171). Both evaluations support the behavioral evidence and mechanistic interpretation involving ovipositor sensilla. Peer review also connects to broader ecological strategies.
Strong alignment on background/contextual claims (C1-C11, C36). Both evaluations accept these as appropriately cited established facts providing necessary context for the study.
Alignment on methodological and contextual claims (C12-C13, C16). OpenEval groups field collection methods separately, while peer review combines with biological control context (C173-C177).
Strong alignment on comparative genomic context (C37-C38, C42-C44). Both evaluations accept these citations to prior work as appropriate for contextualizing Td genome findings.
Alignment on basic biological information (C58-C61). Both evaluations accept these as straightforward observational or established facts providing necessary background.
Alignment on background information about Timps and trypsins (C73-C74, C96). Both evaluations accept these citations as providing important context for interpreting functional roles.
Strong alignment on comparative parasitoid context (C131-C133, C140-C143). Both evaluations accept these citations as essential background for understanding novelty and significance of findings.
Alignment on competition strategy background (C156-C159, C165-C166). Both evaluations accept these as appropriate context for interpreting ecological findings about competitive strategies.

Strong alignment on biological control implications (C172-C177). Both evaluations support the application potential, with peer review explicitly noting the study could help future biological control developments.

Good alignment on high-level summary claims (C17-C20). Both evaluations accept these synthetic conclusions as reasonable interpretations, though peer review groups with broader integrative claims (C136-C139, C170-C171).

Alignment on summary of molecular adaptations (C144-C146). OpenEval groups these as separate summary claims, while peer review integrates them with detailed venom and teratocyte findings, showing different organizational approaches.

Peer review identifies specific claims about venom mechanism inferences (C66, C148, C149) as appropriately qualified speculations. OpenEval addresses these claims within broader result groups (R4, R3) rather than as a separate evaluation.
